title: What implements sandboxed execution, and which tier first?
statement: REQ-0005 requires claims to be testable by execution in a real environment. #56 decides three tiers and #77 decides how they activate, but no controller exists for any of them. Which tier is built first, and what provisions, executes, observes and destroys?
notes: BLOCKING under DEC-0002 — see the earlier note. BOUNDARIES BEFORE MECHANISM (DEC-0003): (a) what may execute — which claims justify running code at all; (b) filesystem, network and credential boundaries per tier (#56), and what a tier may NOT reach; (c) resource limits — time, cost, instance count — since #77's authorisation is meaningless without them; (d) cleanup — #56's `destroy` verb, and what happens when it fails; (e) which observations survive as evidence — commands, output, environment facts, and what is discarded, because #96's applicability filter can only work on facts that were actually captured. Only after those does 'which tier first, implemented how' become answerable.
